summary: Earth Jukebox is a voice-first 3D explorer of Earth and the universe, built for blind and low-vision users. Search for anything, like a solar eclipse, Jupiter or the Earth’s inner core, and it builds a realistic scene from live NASA data. An on-device AI explains it aloud in a natural voice, with no API key needed.
details:
**What it does and how it works:** Earth Jukebox is a voice-first 3D explorer of Earth and the universe. You search for anything, like a solar eclipse, Jupiter or the Earth's inner core. The app fetches live NASA imagery and data, builds a realistic 3D scene with an orbiting camera, and an on-device AI writes a spoken-style briefing from the real NASA facts. A natural neural voice reads it aloud, and you can ask follow-up questions by voice or text.

**Benefits:** NASA's Earth visualizations are almost entirely visual, which excludes blind and low-vision users. Earth Jukebox lets anyone explore Earth science by listening, with keyboard and screen-reader support. It needs no account, no API key and no server.

**Intended impact:** To make NASA Earth science accessible to everyone, and to show how on-device AI and neural voice can open visual data to blind and low-vision people. Next steps are sonifying the EIC frames themselves, more datasets, and more languages.

**Tools and technologies:** React, Vite and Three.js for the app and 3D scenes. WebLLM running Qwen2.5 on-device with WebGPU for the AI. Kokoro neural text-to-speech and the Web Speech API for voice. ARIA labels and keyboard controls for accessibility. Hosted on Vercel. Built with OpenCode.

**Creativity:** Instead of a fixed set of scenes, any search is turned into a real NASA-based 3D scene. The AI and voice run entirely in the browser, and the camera orbits on its own with hold-to-scrub, so nobody gets lost.

**Factors we considered:** Accessibility first, accuracy by grounding the AI in real NASA data, privacy because nothing leaves the device, and fallbacks for devices without WebGPU.
